note_claims.claim: Routine lithium monitoring review for bipolar affective disorder.
Patient reports stable mood and good energy.
Wife reports reduced sleep (about 5 hours) and increased talkativeness and new projects over the last week, which preceded his previous relapse.
Patient denies racing thoughts or overspending.
Patient has no missed lithium doses.
Patient took naproxen (his brother's) for back pain for 3–4 days last week, initially recalled as ibuprofen.
Patient denies diarrhoea, vomiting, unsteadiness, or confusion.
Patient has a long-standing fine tremor in both hands, which is unchanged.
Patient has good fluid intake.
Patient is taking Priadel (lithium carbonate) 800 mg at night.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Fine tremor of both hands is present and unchanged.
Patient's gait is steady.
Lithium level last month was 0.7 mmol/L (12-hour post-dose), which is in range.
eGFR is 74, which is stable.
Thyroid function and calcium are normal.
Possible early signs of hypomanic relapse reported by wife.
Continue Priadel 800 mg at night.
Repeat lithium level in 1 week (12 hours post-dose) due to NSAID exposure, then 3-monthly.
Avoid NSAIDs; paracetamol is fine for back pain.
Inform community mental health team.
Patient must keep a sleep diary and contact care coordinator if sleeping less than five hours for two consecutive nights.
If vomiting, diarrhoea, coarse tremor, unsteadiness, or confusion occurs, stop lithium and seek an urgent lithium level or attend A&E.
Avoid dehydration, especially in hot weather.

transcript_facts.fact: Clinician greeted Mr Fairweather-Okoro and his wife.
Patient identified herself as Adaeze.
Relative greeted the clinician.
Clinician asked if it was okay for Adaeze to stay.
Patient confirmed she was okay with staying.
Clinician initiated the routine lithium review.
Patient reported mood has been steady and work is going well.
Clinician asked about sleep.
Patient reported feeling fine.
Relative reported that the patient has been sleeping less this last week (five hours, maybe) and has been talking a lot more and starting lots of projects, which started the previous relapse.
Patient reported feeling well and having loads of energy.
Clinician asked if the patient was having any racing thoughts or spending more money than usual.
Patient denied racing thoughts or overspending.
Clinician asked if the patient was on Priadel, 800 milligrams at night.
Patient confirmed she was on Priadel, 800 milligrams at night.
Clinician asked about missed doses.
Patient confirmed she has never missed a dose.
Clinician asked if the patient had taken any other medicines recently, including anything from the chemist.
Patient initially stated she took ibuprofen for her back, but corrected herself to naproxen, which her brother gave her.
Clinician asked how many days she took the medication for.
Patient stated she took it for three or four days.
Clinician noted that anti-inflammatory painkillers can raise lithium levels and asked about diarrhoea or vomiting.
Patient denied diarrhoea or vomiting.
Clinician asked if the patient was feeling unsteady on her feet or muddled.
Patient denied feeling unsteady on her feet or muddled.
Clinician asked about any change in her tremor.
Patient reported no change in her tremor, stating it is the same little shake she has always had.
Clinician asked if the patient was drinking plenty of fluids.
Patient confirmed she has a big water bottle at work.
Clinician asked about other medicines and allergies.
Patient stated she has no other medicines and no allergies.
Clinician reviewed blood tests: lithium level last month was 0.7 mmol/L (12-hour post-dose), eGFR is 74 (stable), and thyroid and calcium are normal.
Patient responded positively to the lab results.
Clinician examined the patient's hands and noted a fine tremor in both hands, which is the same as before, and confirmed the patient was walking steadily.
Patient responded with 'Okay'.
Clinician planned to recheck the lithium level in one week (12 hours post-dose) because of naproxen exposure, and then follow up every three months.
Patient agreed to the plan.
Clinician advised the patient not to take ibuprofen or naproxen, suggesting paracetamol for back pain.
Patient acknowledged the advice.

Clinician planned to inform the community mental health team, ask the patient to keep a sleep diary, and instruct them to contact the care coordinator or the clinic if they sleep less than five hours for two nights running.
Relative stated she would keep an eye on the patient.

Clinician instructed the patient to continue Priadel at the same dose and provided safety-netting advice: if vomiting, diarrhoea, coarse shaking, unsteadiness, or confusion occurs, the patient should stop lithium and seek an urgent lithium level or go to A&E.
Patient acknowledged the safety instructions.
Clinician advised the patient to try not to get dehydrated, especially in hot weather.
